newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan EVA Airway to buy US$1 bln planes - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan EVA Airway to buy US$1 bln planes - paper.

text.p: Taiwan's EVA Airways, a unit of shipping giant Evergreen Marine, will soon announce a purchase of aircraft worth more than US$1 billion, the Econonic Daily News reported on Thursday.
EVA spokesman Nieh Kuo-wei would not comment on the report, but said the airline would have an announcement soon.
"Our policy is to give no comment today (Thursday), but we plan to give explanation on Friday or Saturday," Nieh said.
General Electric Co on Monday said its engine unit had a new US$750 million EVA order for 82 GE CF6-80 turbofan engines, suitable for Boeing or McDonnell Douglas planes.
The Economic Daily News quoted unnamed sources as saying the GE announcement indicated EVA soon would unveil a plan to buy at least six mid- and long-haul passenger and cargo planes.
The sources did not say which planemaker would be selected.
EVA said in May it was considering buying 10 or more Boeing 747-500 passenger planes, worth some US$200 million each.

EVA now owns 28 planes -- 12 Boeing 747-400s for long-haul international routes, five Boeing 767-300s, four Boeing 767-200s, six McDonnell Douglas MD-11s and one newly delivered MD-90. EVA took deliver in October of the first of six MD-90 planes bought from McDonnell Douglas Corp in 1995.
The carrier, Taiwan's second international airline, made a net profit of T$198 million in 1995 after four years of losses since it began operations in 1991.
In 1995, EVA made a net profit of T$198 million on sales of T$28.86 billion, compared with a loss of T$950 million in 1994 on sales of T$19 billion, Nieh said.
For 1996, EVA has set a net profit target of some T$600 million on sales of T$35 billion, Nieh said.
EVA has forecast three straight years of profits and plans to listed in the local stock market in 1998, he said.
